capabilities.audience: AI coding agents and automation tools that need to discover how to use exodusii without loading the full documentation corpus.

format.query_command: python -m exodusii learn capabilities [QUERY]  |  python -m exodusii learn skills [QUERY [PATH]]
format.query_language: Lightweight path syntax: whole object with '.', dotted object keys, bracketed object keys, and list indexes. This is not jq.
format.progressive_disclosure: Top-level objects are compact indexes. Query deeper paths for operational details.

overview.what_is_exodusii: exodusii is a Python interface for reading, writing, comparing, querying, and inspecting Sandia Exodus II finite-element databases stored as NetCDF files.
core_use_cases: Inspect mesh and result metadata from finite-element simulations.
Read nodal, element, global, edge, face, and set variables.
Query result variables at selected time steps.
Compare two Exodus databases with exodiff-style tolerance checking.
Compute simple mesh geometry quantities such as centers, volumes, and nodal volumes.
Expose JSON output for AI agents and automation tools.
Compute statistics (mean, max, min, sum, count, std) of a field variable inside a geometric region with optional field-threshold predicate.
Compute material mass inside a geometric region (sum of element_volume * density [* volfrac]).
Read global scalars quickly from one small decomposed piece file without opening the full joined database.
common_agent_queries: python -m exodusii query mesh.exo --select n/TEMP --time last
python -m exodusii stats mesh.exo --select e/ENERGY --time last --by-block
python -m exodusii region-stats mesh.exo --select e/YIELD_STRESS_2 --cylinder 0 0 0 0.05 0 0 0.013 --reduce mean,max --time last

concepts.exodus_database: An Exodus II database is a NetCDF file containing finite-element mesh topology, sets, blocks, coordinates, time values, and result variables.

entities.global: Whole-database result variables, usually one value per time step.
entities.node: Nodal result variables, one value per node per time step.
entities.element: Element result variables, usually stored by element block.
entities.edge: Edge result variables, stored by edge block when edge entities exist.
entities.face: Face result variables, stored by face block when face entities exist.
entities.element_block: A group of elements with the same element type and connectivity width.
entities.edge_block: A group of edges with the same edge topology.
entities.face_block: A group of faces with the same face topology.
entities.node_set: A set of nodes, optionally with distribution factors.
entities.side_set: A set of element-side pairs, optionally with distribution factors.
entities.edge_set: A set of edges, optionally with orientations and distribution factors.
entities.face_set: A set of faces, optionally with orientations and distribution factors.
entities.element_set: A set of elements, optionally with distribution factors.

entity_aliases.summary: All entity-accepting API methods pass the string through a normalizer that strips, lowercases, and replaces hyphens/spaces with underscores. The following aliases are accepted.

time_indexing.python_api: Modern API time indexes are zero-based when integers are used.
time_indexing.legacy_api: Legacy ExodusIIFile-style methods usually use one-based time_step arguments.
time_indexing.cli: The agent CLI accepts first, last, index:N, step:N, or a physical float time.
time_indexing.time_selector_type: The TimeSelector type (core/time.py) accepts: None (full history), 'first', 'last', int (zero-based index), or float (nearest physical time).

connectivity_indexing.modern_api_default: Modern reader methods return one-based connectivity by default.
connectivity_indexing.zero_based_option: Many methods accept zero_based=True to return Python-friendly zero-based connectivity.

commands.summary: Two types of CLI are available. (1) The agent-oriented subcommand CLI: 'python -m exodusii COMMAND ...', prints JSON by default. (2) Two registered console scripts: 'exodiff' and 'exoread'.

learn.purpose: Query static exodusii capabilities and skills for self-learning.

inspect.purpose: Print an agent-friendly summary of one Exodus database.

blocks.purpose: Print element, edge, and face block metadata.

sets.purpose: Print node, side, edge, face, and element set metadata.

query.purpose: Query result variables from a database and emit JSON records.
examples: python -m exodusii query mesh.exo --select n/TEMP --time last --limit 10
python -m exodusii query mesh.exo --select e/ENERGY --time step:5 --limit 10

stats.purpose: Compute compact numeric summaries for selected variables.
examples: python -m exodusii stats mesh.exo --select n/TEMP --time last
python -m exodusii stats mesh.exo --select e/ENERGY --time last --by-block
python -m exodusii stats mesh.exo --select ns/NSVAR --time last --by-set

exodiff.purpose: Compare two Exodus databases with exodiff-style tolerance checking. Registered console script (not a subcommand of 'python -m exodusii'). Returns POSIX exit codes: 0 same, 1 error, 2 different.

tolerance_flags.--floor VALUE: Floor below which values are treated as equal.

time_flags.--start N|LAST: First file-2 step to compare (1-based). 'LAST' compares only the final step on each file.
time_flags.--time-scale S: Multiply file-1 times by S before matching.
time_flags.--time-offset O: Add O to file-1 times before matching.
time_flags.--interpolate: Linearly interpolate file-2 values to each file-1 time.

output_flags.--show-all: Report every compared variable, not only those exceeding tolerance.

exodiff.limitation: Supports matched mesh ordering (default) and coordinate-based mesh matching (--match-coordinates / DiffOptions(coordinate_matching=True)). See python_api.diff for matching options.

exoread.purpose: Interactive extraction of named variables by entity. Registered console script.
exoread.note: Use 'exoread --help' for full flag list. Supports -g/-e/-n/-f/-d entity selectors, -t time, -i index, and -L lineout options.

json_format.terse: Use --terse for compact JSON with separators(',', ':').

query.summary: The database query command extracts result variables from Exodus databases. The static learn query path extracts information from installed JSON capability datasets.

special_node_selectors.n/displacements: Nodal displacement vectors when displacement variables are present.

lineouts.summary: A Lineout extracts a 1-D profile from multi-dimensional tabular mesh data by FIXING one or two coordinate axes (within a tolerance) and SORTING the surviving rows along the remaining free axis. Use it for axial profiles (e.g. down a penetration axis) or radial/cross-section profiles of a field.
lineouts.import: from exodusii.api.lineout import Lineout, lineout  # 'lineout' is a keyword-only factory

axis_spec.float: A float FIXES that axis: only rows within tol of the value are kept and that coordinate column is dropped.
axis_spec.lowercase_name: The string 'x' (or 'y'/'z') marks that axis as the FREE sweep axis: rows are sorted ascending along it and the column is kept.
axis_spec.uppercase_name: The string 'X' (or 'Y'/'Z') is the free sweep axis using DISPLACED coordinates (material + displacement); requires displacement columns in the data.
axis_spec.none: None means the axis is absent or irrelevant.

lineouts.tol: Absolute spatial tolerance for the fixed-axis match. If None, computed automatically as 1e-4 * max(extent_of_fixed_axis, 1e-30) from the data bounding box. For an ELEMENT-center lineout the fixed axis rarely lands exactly on a value, so set tol to about half the local cell size (e.g. tol=3e-4 for a 0.4 mm mesh) so a row of cells is captured; the auto tolerance can be too tight and return zero rows.
lineouts.apply: lo.apply(header, data) -> (new_header, new_data): header is a list of column names, data is a 2-D float array whose columns include coordinate columns named COORDX/COORDY/COORDZ (or LOCATIONX/... after displacement). Also accepts a single structured array: lo.apply(structured) -> structured. Rows are filtered to the line and sorted along the free axis.
lineouts.coordinate_columns: apply() locates coordinate columns by name (COORDX/COORDY/COORDZ or LOCATIONX/Y/Z); an optional leading 'INDEX' column is tolerated. Build your data table with these coordinate column names to use a lineout.
python_examples: lo = Lineout(y=0.0, z=0.0)          # fix y=z=0, sweep along x (axial profile down the x-axis)
lo = Lineout(x=0.006, z=0.0)        # fix x and z, sweep along y (radial cross-section at x=6mm)
lo = Lineout(x=1.0, y='Y', z=0.0)   # sweep along DISPLACED y at fixed x,z
lineouts.cli_form: CLI/exoread lineout strings mirror exoread -L: 'x/1.0' (sweep x with y fixed at 1.0), '1.0/Y/3.0/T0.1' (sweep displaced y, fix x=1.0 and z=3.0, tol=0.1). Trailing 't'/'T' token sets tolerance. Parse with Lineout.from_cli(str).
lineouts.cli_status: The JSON `query` CLI may or may not wire lineout in this build; the Python Lineout.apply path always works. For a lineout of results, assemble a table of [coords..., field] with COORDX/Y/Z column names (element lineout: use entity_centers as the coordinates) and call apply().
recipe_element_field_lineout: import numpy as np; from exodusii.api.file import ExodusFile; from exodusii.mesh import entity_centers; from exodusii.api.lineout import Lineout
c=entity_centers(conn, coords); f=exo.values('TEMPERATURE_2', on='element', block_id=bid, time='last')
hdr, prof = Lineout(y=0.0, z=0.0).apply(header, data)   # axial temperature profile vs x
# prof columns are [COORDX, TEMPERATURE_2], sorted by x
# if prof has 0 rows, widen tol (element centers rarely sit exactly on y=z=0): Lineout(y=0.0, z=0.0, tol=3e-4)

python_api.summary: The modern API is centered on ExodusFile for reading, ExodusWriter for writing, ParallelExodusFile for aggregating decomposed files, and diff/DiffOptions for comparison.

open.example:
with ExodusFile.open('mesh.exo') as exo:
    print(exo.title)
    print(exo.dimension)

methods: exo.variable_truth_table('element', id=block_id)  # returns (num_vars,) int64 row or (num_blocks, num_vars) full table

values.signature: exo.values(name, *, on, time=None, block_id=None, block=None, set_id=None)
notes: All parameters after 'name' are keyword-only.
'on' is required and accepts any entity alias string (see .concepts.entity_aliases).
'block' is an alias for 'block_id'; if both are given, 'block_id' wins.
time=None returns full time history; shape depends on entity.
For element variables with block_id=None, values across all blocks are concatenated.
examples: exo.values('ENERGY', on='element', time='last')  # all blocks concatenated

coordinates.storage_note: Supports both large-model (coordx/coordy/coordz) and normal-model (combined 'coord' variable) NetCDF storage formats.

truth_table.behavior: Returns a (num_blocks, num_vars) int64 array when id is None, or a (num_vars,) row for one block when id is given. When no explicit truth table is stored, the table is derived dynamically by probing per-block NetCDF variables (matches SEACAS ex_get_truth_table.c behavior). Returns None only for entity types that do not support a truth table (e.g. global).
examples: row = exo.variable_truth_table('element', id=10)  # row for block 10

parallel.example:
with ParallelExodusFile.open('mesh.e.2.0', 'mesh.e.2.1') as exo:
    coords = exo.coordinates()
    values = exo.values('TEMP', on='node', time='last')
parallel.id_maps: Aggregation uses node_num_map / elem_num_map / edge_num_map / face_num_map from each component file. If a map is absent, a sequential fallback is used and a UserWarning is emitted. The fallback is correct only for non-overlapping partitions; real Nemesis files with shared nodes must include node_num_map.

writer.creation: ExodusWriter.create(path)  # classmethod, use as context manager
workflow_order: 1. writer.initialize(title, dimension, node_count, element_count, element_blocks=N, node_sets=M, side_sets=K, ...)  # MUST be first; declares all upfront counts
5. writer.define_element_block(block_id, element_type, connectivity)  # for each block
6. writer.define_node_set(set_id, nodes, distribution_factors=None)  # for each node set
7. writer.define_side_set(set_id, elements, sides, distribution_factors=None)  # for each side set
11. writer.write_time(t)  # call once per time step; returns 1-based step number
12. writer.write_global_values([v1, v2])  # all globals at once per step
writer.initialize_signature: writer.initialize(title, dimension, node_count, element_count, *, element_blocks=0, node_sets=0, side_sets=0, edge_count=0, edge_blocks=0, face_count=0, face_blocks=0, edge_sets=0, face_sets=0, element_sets=0, floating_point_word_size=8)
writer.critical_constraint: The counts passed to initialize() (element_blocks, node_sets, etc.) must exactly match the number of blocks/sets subsequently defined. NetCDF4 dimensions cannot be resized after creation. Passing the wrong count raises ExodusWriteError.
writer.define_element_block_signature: writer.define_element_block(block_id, element_type, connectivity, *, name='', zero_based=False, active=True)
writer.minimal_example:
with ExodusWriter.create('out.exo') as w:
    w.initialize('title', 2, 4, 1, element_blocks=1)
    w.write_coordinates([[0,0],[1,0],[1,1],[0,1]])
    w.define_element_block(10, 'quad', [[1,2,3,4]])
    w.define_node_variables(['TEMP'])
    w.write_time(0.0)
    w.write_node_values('TEMP', [100, 200, 300, 400])

diff.summary: The diff API compares two Exodus databases with exodiff-style tolerance semantics. All symbols are importable from the top-level exodusii package.
diff.import: from exodusii import diff, DiffOptions, DiffResult, VariableDiff, TimeSelection, Tolerance, ToleranceMode
diff.diff_accepts: file1 and file2 can be paths (str or Path) or open ExodusFile objects.

fields.same: bool — True when no structural error and no variable exceeded tolerance.
fields.errors: list[str] — fatal structural mismatches (node count, missing variables, etc.)
fields.warnings: list[str] — non-fatal notices (time step count mismatch, time value differences)
fields.variable_diffs: list[VariableDiff] — one record per variable/location that exceeded tolerance (or all if show_all=True)
fields.coordinate_max_delta: float | None — worst coordinate difference if coordinates were compared

DiffResult.bool_behavior: bool(result) is True when result.same is True.

fields.name: str — variable name
fields.max_delta: float — worst delta found; inf for NaN mismatch or shape mismatch
fields.exceeded: bool — True when tolerance was exceeded
fields.time_index: int | None — zero-based time step of worst value
fields.entry_index: int | None — entry position of worst value
fields.value1: float | None — file1 value at worst location
fields.value2: float | None — file2 value at worst location

DiffOptions.summary: Frozen dataclass controlling all comparison behavior.

key_fields.default_tolerance: Tolerance — applied when no per-category or per-variable override exists. Default: Tolerance(RELATIVE, 1e-6).
key_fields.time_tolerance: Tolerance — for time value matching. Default: Tolerance(RELATIVE, 1e-6, floor=1e-15).
Tolerance | None — per-category overrides; None falls back to default_tolerance.
key_fields.variable_tolerances: Mapping[str, Tolerance] — per-variable name overrides, highest priority.
key_fields.ignore_case: bool — case-insensitive variable name matching (default True).
key_fields.time_step_offset: int — legacy scalar offset; prefer time_selection for full control.
key_fields.time_selection: TimeSelection | None — full time-step selection and interpolation settings.
key_fields.compare_attributes: bool — compare block element attributes (default True).
key_fields.show_all: bool — include within-tolerance records in variable_diffs (default False).

TimeSelection.summary: Frozen dataclass for time-step range and interpolation control. All step numbers are 1-based and refer to file-2.

fields.start: int — first file-2 step (1-based, default 1). -1 = LAST: compare only the final step on each file.
fields.stop: int — last file-2 step inclusive (-1 = all, default -1).
fields.time_value_scale: float — multiply file-1 times before matching (default 1.0).
fields.time_value_offset: float — add to file-1 times before matching (default 0.0).
fields.interpolating: bool — linearly interpolate file-2 values to each file-1 time (default False). Steps outside file-2 time range are skipped.

examples:
opts = DiffOptions(
    nodal_tolerance=Tolerance(ToleranceMode.RELATIVE, 1e-6),
    variable_tolerances={'PRESSURE': Tolerance(ToleranceMode.ABSOLUTE, 1e-4)},
    exclude=frozenset({'TIME'})
)
result = diff('gold.exo', 'test.exo', opts)

opts = DiffOptions(time_selection=TimeSelection(start=3, stop=10, increment=2))
result = diff('gold.exo', 'test.exo', opts)
result = diff('gold.exo', 'reordered.exo', opts)  # files with different node/elem order

coordinate_matching.summary: Enable with DiffOptions(coordinate_matching=True). Builds a permutation map from spatial coordinates before comparison. Allows comparing files whose nodes/elements are in different order but describe the same physical mesh.

options.matching_tolerance: float — per-axis spatial proximity tolerance for building the map (default 1e-6). Independent of coordinate_tolerance.
options.require_unique_mapping: bool — raise MeshMatchError on unmatched nodes/elements (default True). Set False to warn and continue with partial map.

result_fields.mesh_map_built: bool — True when the coordinate-based map was successfully built.
result_fields.unmatched_nodes: int — count of unmatched nodes (0 unless require_unique_mapping=False).

coordinate_matching.sideset_note: Sideset face ordinals are checked after element remapping; ordinal mismatches are emitted as warnings in result.warnings but are not fatal errors.

diff.limitation: Matched ordering is the default. Coordinate matching requires equal node and element counts in both files. Full face-ordinal correction from connectivity permutation is not performed.

compare.summary: Simple mesh/value similarity checks (not full exodiff-style tolerance comparison).
compare.note: For full per-variable tolerance checking with result reporting, use diff() instead.

mesh_geometry.summary: exodusii.mesh provides finite-element geometry helpers, geometric region predicates, and coordinate-based mesh matching. Use this for spatial (geometry-based) selection and reduction of results: compute element centers, select cells inside a shape (Cylinder/Sphere/Circle/Rectangle/Quad), compute per-element volumes, and mass- or volume-weight results. This is the correct, source-free reference for all geometry queries; you do NOT need to read the exodusii source.

imports.helpers: from exodusii.mesh import entity_centers, element_volumes, nodal_volumes, connected_average, bounding_box, characteristic_element_length
imports.regions: from exodusii.mesh import Cylinder, Sphere, Circle, Rectangle, Quad  # also: from exodusii.mesh.regions import ...  or  from exodusii.region import ...
imports.region_factories: from exodusii.mesh import cylinder, sphere, circle, rectangle, quad  # lowercase factory functions, same args as the classes
imports.time_domains: from exodusii.mesh import BoundedTimeDomain, UnboundedTimeDomain, bounded_time_domain, unbounded_time_domain
imports.note: Region classes are re-exported from three places (exodusii.mesh, exodusii.mesh.regions, exodusii.region) and are identical. All region and helper functions are pure NumPy and do not need an open file.

entity_centers.purpose: Element centroids: mean of the element's node coordinates. Feed the result to region.contains() to classify cells geometrically.
entity_centers.conn: ZERO-BASED connectivity, shape (n_elems, n_nodes_per_elem). Get it via exo.element_connectivity(block_id, zero_based=True).
entity_centers.coords: Nodal coordinates, shape (n_nodes, dim). Get it via exo.coordinates(). Use exo.coordinates(time='last', displaced=True) for deformed geometry.

element_volumes.purpose: Per-element measure: volume for 3-D element types, area for 2-D. Multiply by DENSITY (and/or volume fraction) and sum over a region to get a true mass inside that region (e.g. an ejected plug mass) instead of relying on whole-block global sums.
element_volumes.element_type: Exodus element-type string, e.g. 'hex8', 'quad4', 'tet4', 'wedge6' (see .element_type_aliases; matching is case-insensitive and accepts the block's own name). Get a block's type directly with exo.element_block(block_id).element_type (this returns the stored Exodus name, e.g. 'HEX', which element_volumes accepts as-is).
element_volumes.note: Values are signed; take np.abs if node ordering may be inverted.

nodal_volumes.signature: nodal_volumes(element_type, conn, coords, *, num_nodes=None) -> ndarray, shape (n_nodes,)
nodal_volumes.purpose: Distribute each element's measure equally to its nodes; useful for nodal mass/volume weighting.

connected_average.purpose: Average a nodal field over each element's connectivity, i.e. interpolate nodal values to element centers.

bounding_box.purpose: Axis-aligned bounding box of a coordinate array; handy for choosing region parameters or lineout fixed values.

characteristic_element_length.purpose: Representative element size per element (e.g. for mesh-resolution or shear-band-width diagnostics).

regions.summary: Geometric predicate objects. Construct with world coordinates, then call region.contains(points) where points is (n, dim) or a single (dim,) point. Returns a boolean mask (or bool for a single point). Combine masks with numpy &, |, ~. Feed entity_centers(...) as points to select ELEMENTS by centroid, or coords to select NODES.
regions.contains: region.contains(points) -> ndarray[bool] of shape (n,), or a Python bool for a single point. Closed regions (boundary included).

Cylinder.p1_p2: The two endpoints of the cylinder AXIS (world coordinates, 2-D or 3-D, must match and be distinct).
Cylinder.behavior: 3-D: finite circular cylinder about the p1->p2 segment; containment is distance-to-segment <= radius (endpoints get spherical-cap inclusion). 2-D: a capsule around the segment.

Quad.note: Closed 2-D quadrilateral defined by four vertices (point-in-polygon test).

regions.hollow_shell_recipe: For an annulus/tube (e.g. a shear band at a fixed radius range on a cylindrical surface), subtract two cylinders: inside = Cylinder(p1,p2,r_outer).contains(c) & ~Cylinder(p1,p2,r_inner).contains(c).
regions.time_domains: BoundedTimeDomain(lower, upper) and UnboundedTimeDomain expose contains(times) for temporal masking (either bound may be None for semi-bounded).

hollow_rim_band: rim = outer & ~inner                              # cells in the 7-13 mm shell
band = rim & (eqps > 0.5)                         # combine geometry with a field threshold
mass_inside_region: vol = element_volumes(etype, conn, coords)        # per-element volume
vfrac = exo.values('VOLFRC_2', on='element', block_id=bid, time='last')  # if mixed cells
# multiply by any symmetry factor (e.g. x4 for a quarter model) for the full-model mass
notes: Always pass ZERO-BASED connectivity to the mesh helpers (zero_based=True).
entity_centers -> region.contains selects by ELEMENT centroid; pass exo.coordinates() directly to region.contains to select NODES.
Regions use the SAME units as the mesh coordinates (usually meters). Confirm with bounding_box(coords).
For decomposed parallel output, do this per piece and OR/concatenate, or open with ParallelExodusFile first (see .python_api.parallel).
Prefer per-region element_volumes*density sums for masses; the global MAT_MASS_* / block totals average the whole block and mislead for localized features.

functions.entity_centers: Compute element centers from zero-based connectivity and coordinates. See .helper_functions.entity_centers.
functions.element_volumes: Compute per-element areas (2-D) or volumes (3-D). See .helper_functions.element_volumes.
functions.nodal_volumes: Distribute element measures to nodes. See .helper_functions.nodal_volumes.
functions.connected_average: Average nodal values over connectivity. See .helper_functions.connected_average.

matching.build_mesh_map: Build a MeshMap permutation map between two ExodusFile objects by spatial coordinate proximity. Used by diff() when coordinate_matching=True.
matching.MeshMap: Frozen dataclass holding node_map, node_map_inv, elem_map, elem_map_inv, block_map, unmatched_nodes, unmatched_elems.
matching.MeshMatchError: Raised when matching fails and require_unique_mapping=True.
matching.check_sideset_ordinals: Check sideset face ordinals after element remapping; returns list of warning strings.

legacy.summary: The compatibility layer preserves much of the historical ExodusIIFile-style API.
legacy.time_indexing: Legacy methods generally use one-based time_step arguments.

region_reduce.summary: Native spatial reduction over a geometric region with optional field-threshold predicate. Replaces the common pattern of manually computing element centers, building a region mask, AND-ing with a field threshold, and reducing. Available as ExodusFile.region_stats(), ExodusFile.region_mass(), and the CLI subcommand 'python -m exodusii region-stats'.
region_reduce.imports: from exodusii import region_stats, region_mass, RegionStatsResult, RegionMassResult

region_stats.signature: exo.region_stats(name, *, on='element', block_id=None, region, where=None, reduce, time=None, symmetry_factor=1.0) -> RegionStatsResult
notes: region must implement region.contains(points) — use Cylinder, Sphere, Circle, Rectangle, Quad from exodusii.mesh.
where is a safe field-threshold predicate: 'VARNAME OP VALUE' only (e.g. 'EQPS_2 > 1.0'). No arbitrary Python.
symmetry_factor is applied only to extensive reducers (sum, count). Mean, max, min, std are intensive and are NOT scaled.
block_id=None concatenates all element blocks.
time=None selects the last time step.
Returns RegionStatsResult with fields: variable, entity, block_id, time_index, time_value, count_total, count_selected, symmetry_factor, stats.

region_mass.signature: exo.region_mass(*, block_id, region, density_name='DENSITY', volfrac_name=None, where=None, time=None, symmetry_factor=1.0) -> RegionMassResult
region_mass.formula: mass = symmetry_factor * sum(|vol_i| * density_i [* volfrac_i]) over selected elements
notes: element_volumes is computed automatically from the block element type.
volfrac_name is optional; omit for pure materials, set for mixed-material cells.
symmetry_factor=4.0 for a quarter-symmetry model.
Returns RegionMassResult with fields: block_id, time_index, time_value, count_total, count_selected, density_name, volfrac_name, symmetry_factor, mass.

cli_region_stats.command: python -m exodusii region-stats FILE --select ENTITY/NAME --REGION_TYPE ARGS --reduce REDUCERS [--block BLOCK_ID] [--where EXPR] [--time SELECTOR] [--symmetry FACTOR]

region_flags.--cylinder AX AY AZ BX BY BZ R: 3-D cylinder from axis point A to B with radius R.
region_flags.--sphere CX CY CZ R: 3-D sphere centred at (CX,CY,CZ) with radius R.
region_flags.--circle CX CY R: 2-D circle centred at (CX,CY) with radius R.
region_flags.--rectangle OX OY W H: 2-D axis-aligned rectangle origin (OX,OY) width W height H.

examples: python -m exodusii region-stats run.exo --select e/YIELD_STRESS_2 --cylinder 0 0 0 0.05 0 0 0.013 --reduce mean,max,count --time last
python -m exodusii region-stats run.exo --select e/ENERGY --cylinder 0 0 0 0.05 0 0 0.013 --where 'EQPS_2 > 1.0' --reduce mean --time last --block 3
python -m exodusii region-stats run.exo --select e/DENSITY --sphere 0 0 0 0.01 --reduce sum --symmetry 4 --time last

piece_flag_for_globals.summary: The --piece N flag on 'query' and 'stats' subcommands opens only the Nth file argument directly instead of aggregating all component files. Use this to read global scalar variables from one small decomposed component file without opening the full joined (potentially multi-GB) database. Global variables are fully present in every component file.
notes: --piece 0 when a single file path is given: opens that file directly (identical to omitting --piece).
--piece N with a glob pattern: opens the Nth lexicographically sorted match.
Only correct for global variables. Element/nodal variables require all pieces for a correct joined view.
examples: python -m exodusii query run.exo.96.00 --select g/MASSDELETED --time last --piece 0

limitations.exodiff_mesh_matching: The Python exodiff supports both matched mesh ordering (default) and coordinate-based mesh matching (DiffOptions(coordinate_matching=True) / CLI --match-coordinates). See python_api.diff.coordinate_matching for details.
limitations.writer_upfront_counts: ExodusWriter requires exact block/set counts to be declared in initialize() before any blocks or sets are defined. NetCDF4 dimensions cannot be resized after creation. Passing a wrong count raises ExodusWriteError.
limitations.parallel_id_maps: ParallelExodusFile correctness depends on node_num_map / elem_num_map being present in each component file. If absent, a sequential fallback is used and UserWarning is emitted. The fallback is correct only for non-overlapping partitions; files with shared border/external nodes will produce wrong coordinates and connectivity without the maps.
query_cli: Large arrays are truncated by default; use --limit -1 carefully.
Some advanced Exodus entities may require direct Python API access if not exposed through the CLI.
static_capabilities: The static capability dataset is a compact guide, not a full API reference.
